identity_digest_encoding: SHA256 of UTF-8 JSON, sorted keys, compact separators, allow_nan=False
compatibility_basis: Original collector rejects selected unresolved charged-kt forests in 200<=calorimetric_pT<251 before a design checkpoint can commit; an original completed selected reconstruction therefore has one root.

Signed-root execution preserves single-root results. Its successful multi-root branch requires a unique positive root strictly harder in pT than every other root, and therefore selects the same root as FastJet keep_only_hardest without a tie.
Upstream-hardest execution selects through FastJet Recluster.generate_output_jet on the same existing charged-kt roots, with unchanged signed input tracks, recombiner, R=2.5, and Lund grooming.

Changes to outside-window dR12 forests cannot enter the stored selected dR12 histogram. Calorimetric jet pT, charged fraction, other observables, weights, and raw normalization components are unchanged.
All full per-event count arrays, paired fingerprints, sample proofs, original native/source/bootstrap identities, and original job IDs remain in their immutable committed checkpoint files.
Certified restores must validate the file SHA and use the original checkpoint helper with that proof's exact original identity; missing or changed certified files must never be recollected.

audit_scope.original: Selected multi-root cases absent by the original fatal guard; outside-fit remnant audit unavailable.
audit_scope.signed_root: Historical audit covers the earlier signed-root execution only; its fields and metadata must not be rewritten as the general hardest-root audit.
audit_scope.new: General per-event hardest-root/remnant audit, including actual signs, ties, and selected-root p4/m2; no sign, spacelike, or equal-pT veto.

qualifications: Count-level structural compatibility, not a claim of bitwise replay by the new compiled binary.
The inventory verified file SHA and sealed JSON metadata, not all count-array checksums; the original restore helper retains the array/source/pairing/audit validation.
Signed-background reconstruction remains a model-side convention, not an ATLAS requirement.
This certificate is not authorization for staging, jobs, retries, or physics changes.
